title: Psychosis: dopamine and hearing a voice
description: Psychosis is a state in which a person's experience loses touch with shared reality, for example hearing a voice that others do not hear. It is a core feature of schizophrenia and can also happen in other conditions. The episode follows two of the best-studied findings: a raised capacity to produce dopamine in the striatum, which is already present before psychosis begins, and the brain network that is active while a voice is heard. In the striatum, brightness stands for dopamine production measured with tracer scans, not for activity.
caveat: The dopamine findings come from tracer scans comparing groups of people with and without psychosis, and from one small study of people with early warning signs. The voice findings come from a pooled analysis of ten studies, 68 people in all, who heard voices during scanning. These were never one experiment, and the stages are built from different groups of people, not by following individuals. The idea that too much dopamine makes ordinary things feel strangely significant is a proposed framework. People's experiences of psychosis vary widely.

phases.name: Early warning signs
phases.caption: Before psychosis begins, some people have milder unusual experiences. In one study of people at this stage, the capacity to produce dopamine in the associative striatum was already raised, to a level between that of healthy people and people with schizophrenia.

phases.name: Psychosis
phases.caption: In psychosis, dopamine production in the striatum is raised, one of the most consistent findings in this field. A proposed explanation is that too much dopamine gives ordinary experiences and thoughts a feeling of special significance.

order.rationale: The early-sign and psychosis findings come from different groups of people compared at one time point, not from following the same people.

phases.name: Hearing a voice
phases.caption: While a voice is heard, areas that produce and perceive speech become more active: Broca's area, the front of the insula, the temporal cortex, the inferior parietal cortex, and the hippocampus and the cortex around it, which are involved in verbal memory.

order.rationale: The voice findings come from people already experiencing psychosis, scanned while hearing voices. Placing them after the dopamine finding is a way of presenting the two.

phases.name: The voice stops
phases.caption: The voice stops and these areas settle. The raised dopamine production is a longer-lasting state, so it stays.

order.rationale: The studies compare periods with and without voices. The return to rest when a voice stops follows from that design.

regions.explanation: The capacity to produce and release dopamine in the striatum is raised in schizophrenia, with a large effect, in a pooled analysis of 44 studies; dopamine transporters are not changed. In people with early warning signs it is already raised, to an intermediate degree, mainly in the associative striatum. The associative striatum is mostly the caudate, which is drawn; it also includes the front of the putamen. Brightness here stands for dopamine production, not activity.

citations.title: Elevated striatal dopamine function linked to prodromal signs of schizophrenia.
citations.quote: Striatal (18)F-dopa uptake was elevated in patients with prodromal symptoms of schizophrenia (effect size, 0.75) to an intermediate degree compared with that in patients with schizophrenia (effect size, 1.25). The elevation was localized in the associative striatum in both groups.

citations.title: The dopamine hypothesis of schizophrenia: version III--the final common pathway.
citations.quote: This hypothesis seeks to be comprehensive in providing a framework that links risk factors, including pregnancy and obstetric complications, stress and trauma, drug use, and genes, to increased presynaptic striatal dopaminergic function.

regions.explanation: Broca's area and the frontal operculum, which produce speech, are active while a voice is heard, on both sides. They lie in the inferior frontal gyrus, which is drawn.

citations.authors: Jardri R, Pouchet A, Pins D, Thomas P
citations.title: Cortical activations during auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia: a coordinate-based meta-analysis.
citations.quote: Patients experiencing AVHs demonstrated significantly increased activation likelihoods in a bilateral neural network, including the Broca's area (activation likelihood estimation=1.84×10⁻³), anterior insula (1.78×10⁻³), precentral gyrus (1.46×10⁻³), frontal operculum (1.29×10⁻³), middle and superior temporal gyri (1.59×10⁻³), inferior parietal lobule (1.33×10⁻³), and hippocampus/parahippocampal region (1.90×10⁻³).

citations.authors: Jardri R, Pouchet A, Pins D, Thomas P
citations.title: Cortical activations during auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia: a coordinate-based meta-analysis.
